title: Referral price & commission typed on a single-price product are silently thrown away on save
detail: The pricing table's own hint (line 448-451) says "set price, offer, referral & commission for each. Leave Color/Size as '—' for a single-price product." But at save time only rows that pass `isVariantRow` (line 38-39: has a stored variant id, a colorId, a sizeId, or some other attribute) become variants. A single-price row has none of those, so `hasVariants` is false (line 200) and `variants: []` is written (line 264). `referralPricePaise` / `commissionPaise` (lines 256-257) only exist inside a variant object — there is no top-level product field for them and none is written by `saveProduct` (api/products.ts:124-154). Nothing warns the admin; the save reports success. Re-opening the product runs `productToRows` (line 62), which hardcodes `referral: '', comm: ''` for the non-variant branch, so the fields come back blank. No other admin screen edits these fields (grep over admin/src finds referral/commission only in this form and lib/pricing.ts).
failure_scenario: Admin opens a simple product with no colour/size (e.g. a gift card), types Price 2499, Offer 1999, Referral 1799, Comm. 200, clicks "Save changes" and gets the "Changes saved" toast. Firestore stores mrpPaise/offerPricePaise only; referral and commission are gone. Re-opening the product shows both cells empty, and web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:213 (`product.isAffiliateEligible && referralPaise != null`, where referralPaise comes from `variant?.referralPricePaise`) never renders the AFFILIATE box for that product.
fix: Either persist the single-row referral/commission on the product doc (add referralPricePaise/commissionPaise to the Product type + saveProduct and make web/app fall back to them when `variant` is undefined), or disable/grey the Referral and Comm. cells on a row with no Color/Size and explain why.

verdict.reason: Claim holds up. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx, isVariantRow (l.38-39) requires a stored variant id, colorId, sizeId or extra attribute; the single-price row the form's own hint (l.448-451) tells admins to create ("Leave Color/Size as '—' for a single-price product") has none, so hasVariants is false (l.200) and variants: [] is written (l.264). referralPricePaise/commissionPaise are produced only inside the variant map (l.256-257). I confirmed there is no fallback: packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts puts these fields on ProductVariant only (l.40-41) — Product has no top-level equivalent — and saveProduct (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:124-154) never writes them. No other surface supplies them: grep over admin/src finds referral/commission only in this form, lib/pricing.ts (validation, which ironically validates the referral/comm ladder for the row it is about to discard) and csv.ts:128 (passes referral: ''); functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:66-69 accrues from the affiliate's commissionRate and never reads or backfills the variant field. Round-trip loss confirmed by productToRows l.62 hardcoding referral: '', comm: ''. A real consumer exists: web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:113-114 and :214 gate the AFFILIATE box on variant?.referralPricePaise, so a simple product can never display it. Reachable in practice: scripts/seed.ts:330 gives non-clothing products variants: [], and importProducts (api/products.ts:305-306) creates hasVariants: false products. The guard at l.195-204 addresses the inverse bug (wiping an existing variant set) and does not fire here. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Severity is moderate rather than financial (the field is storefront-display only; commission accrual uses the affiliate rate), but it is a genuine, fixable silent data-loss/broken-CRUD defect that reports success.

title: Per-variant commissionPaise is advertised to shoppers as guaranteed earnings but the commission engine never reads it
detail: The form writes `commissionPaise` per variant (line 257) and `saveProduct` persists it (api/products.ts:139). web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:214-223 renders it verbatim: "Referral price ₹X · you earn ₹Y per sale". But the money that is actually paid is computed in functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:66-69 as `Math.floor(eligiblePaise * normaliseRate(affiliate.commissionRate))` — the referring customer's own rate on the whole merchandise value. Grep across functions/src finds zero reads of `variants[].commissionPaise` or of the product-level `affiliateCommissionRate` (which admin always writes as `null`, api/products.ts:181/322). So the number an admin types per variant has no effect on any payout whatsoever, while being shown to affiliates as a promise.
failure_scenario: Admin sets Comm. = ₹200 on the Green/M variant of a ₹1999 product. The storefront product page tells the affiliate "you earn ₹200.00 per sale". A referred customer buys one; placeOrder accrues `1999_00 * affiliate.commissionRate` (5% ⇒ ₹99.95) into `commissions`, and the affiliate dashboard shows ~₹100. The admin-entered ₹200 is never used and the affiliate is under-paid relative to what the storefront promised.
fix: Make accrueCommission prefer the ordered variant's `commissionPaise` (and the product's `affiliateCommissionRate`) when present, falling back to the affiliate rate — or stop writing/displaying per-variant commission and remove the Comm. column and the web "you earn" copy.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real cross-surface defect. Admin ProductFormPage.tsx:257 persists per-variant `commissionPaise`, and web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:113-114,214-223 renders it verbatim as "you earn ₹Y per sale" (gate is effectively always open: admin hardcodes isAffiliateEligible:true at api/products.ts:180/321, and the banner is not restricted to affiliate viewers). The paid amount comes solely from functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:66-68 `Math.floor(eligiblePaise * normaliseRate(affiliate.commissionRate))`, invoked at functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:675-687 with eligiblePaise = subtotal - discount — a whole-order figure with no per-variant or per-product term. Exhaustive greps over functions/src, web/src, app/lib and packages/shared show no reader of variants[].commissionPaise outside the admin form and the web product page (all other commissionPaise hits are the unrelated field on commissions/{id} docs), and product-level affiliateCommissionRate is written as null by all four writers and read by nobody. Reachable in practice: scripts/seed.ts:338-339 populates both fields. Not on the already-fixed list; the "payouts are deliberately manual" exemption covers bank transfer, not accrual, which is automated. Only nuance: seed values coincidentally equal 5% of offer price, hiding the divergence in demo data for single-item, discount-free orders; any admin-typed value or multi-item/discounted cart diverges.

title: Failed/timed-out adjustStock call leaves the deltas loaded → a retry applies the same stock delta twice
detail: `adminAdjustStock` mutates stock relatively (`after = Math.max(0, before + delta)`, functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:81 and :92) and carries NO idempotency key — the payload has only {productId, variantId, delta}. The client acknowledges this risk for exactly one path: `LedgerWriteError` (api/inventory.ts:58-63, 128-134), where it clears `deltas` so Save can't re-fire. Every OTHER failure falls into the `else` at AdjustStockPage.tsx:99-101, which shows the generic toast 'Could not save adjustments.' and leaves `deltas` fully populated and the Save button re-enabled. `httpsCallable` throws identically for 'the transaction never ran' and 'the transaction committed but the response was lost' (deadline-exceeded / internal / network drop), so the screen invites the operator to redo a write that already landed.
failure_scenario: Admin sets +50 on SKU PERF-AMB-50 (stock 10) and clicks Save. The callable commits the transaction (stock now 60) but the HTTP response is lost on a flaky connection. The toast reads 'Could not save adjustments.', the stepper still shows +50, so the admin clicks Save again. Stock becomes 110 and two ledger rows appear (10→60 and 60→110) for one physical delivery of 50 units.
fix: Give the callable an idempotency key: have the client generate a UUID per Save, pass it in the payload, and have adminAdjustStock record/short-circuit on `stockAdjustmentBatches/{key}` inside the same transaction. Failing that, clear `deltas` and force a reload on ANY error from `adjustStock`, and tell the operator to re-check the current stock before adjusting again.

verdict.reason: Every factual element checks out. adminAdjustStock mutates stock relatively (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:81, :92) and its zod schema (lines 11-23) carries no nonce/idempotency field, so a replay compounds the delta. The client (admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:52-57) documents this exact hazard in a comment — "no idempotency key, so the caller must NOT offer a plain retry" — but wires the mitigation only into the ledger-batch catch (128-134, clearing deltas via LedgerWriteError). AdjustStockPage.tsx:99-101 handles every other failure with a generic toast, leaves `deltas` fully populated, and `finally` (102-104) re-enables Save. Firebase callables are a single POST with no auto-retry, so "transaction committed but response lost" (network drop / deadline-exceeded) is indistinguishable from "never ran", and the screen invites a human retry that double-applies. No server-side re-check, no reconciliation from stockAdjustments (explicitly "history, not the source of truth"), and the live product snapshot is incidental UX rather than a guard. The page is routed (admin/src/app/router.tsx:72). Not on the already-fixed list (which covers only the {before,after} return values) nor the known-intentional list. Fixable with an in-repo pattern: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:437-446 already claims idempotencyKeys/{uid}__{hash} inside the transaction from a client nonce. One caveat on framing: the correct fix is that server-side nonce, NOT clearing deltas in the else branch — most errors reaching it (not-found batch rejection at inventory.ts:108-113, permission-denied, invalid-argument) are definite non-commits where retry is the intended remedy. Confidence is medium because the trigger window is narrow (response lost after commit) and the claim anchors the fix at the wrong layer, but the underlying correctness gap is real.

title: Saving a product from the Products form writes back the variant stock snapshot taken when the form opened, silently reverting inventory adjustments
detail: `existingRef.current` is loaded exactly once per mount (ProductFormPage.tsx:107-135 — a `getProduct` inside a useEffect keyed on [isNew, routeId, navigate], not a live subscription). At save time each variant is rebuilt with `stock: prev?.stock ?? 0` where `prev` comes from that stale ref, and saveProduct writes the whole array (`variants: values.variants`, products/api/products.ts:138). Nothing merges or re-reads stock at commit time, and the rule `products/{id}: allow write: if canWrite('products')` lets that client write through. Every stock change made after the form opened — an adminAdjustStock adjustment, a placeOrder decrement, a cancel restock — is overwritten.
failure_scenario: Admin A opens 'Amber Oud 50ml' to fix a typo in the description at 10:00. At 10:05 Admin B receives 200 units and adjusts variant AMB-50 from 12 → 212 in Inventory (the stockAdjustments ledger records 12→212). At 10:10 Admin A clicks Save. The variants array is written with stock: 12. Inventory now shows 12 again, the history modal still shows the 212 entry, and 200 units of real inventory are invisible to the storefront.
fix: Re-read the product inside a transaction at save time and merge only the form-owned variant fields (price/label/sku/attributes), never `stock`; or move the variants write into a callable that patches per-field instead of replacing the array.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real and fixable. `existingRef.current` in /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx is a mount-time snapshot (one-shot `getProduct` in a useEffect keyed [isNew, routeId, navigate], line 107-136; no live subscription writes to it). At save, line 252 emits `stock: prev?.stock ?? 0` (plus weight/visibility at 258-259) from that snapshot, and saveProduct's edit branch does a whole-array replace via `variants: values.variants` (products.ts:139, spread into updateDoc at line 198) with no stock merge — even though it already re-reads the doc at line 197 for bestSellerOrder/publishedAt, so the fresh data is right there. No server guard: firestore.rules:50-52 is an unrestricted `allow write: if canWrite('products')`, and there is no product document trigger in functions/src. Stock genuinely lives in the clobbered array: adminAdjustStock rewrites `update.variants` with `{...v, stock: after}` (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:86-96), placeOrder decrements `v.stock` (orders/checkout.ts:559-560), cancel restocks it (orders/cancel.ts:119). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Decisive counter-evidence to "intended": the identical stale-write hazard was explicitly recognised and fixed for the rating aggregate in this same function (ratingPatch, lines 213-222, and the ProductFormValues doc comment at products.ts:106-113) — stock simply did not get the same treatment. Only refinement to the claim: non-variant products are unaffected (top-level `stock` is not part of the edit payload); the loss is limited to variant products, which is the scenario described.

title: Adding the first variant to an existing simple product wipes its stock to zero
detail: Save flips `hasVariants` to true as soon as one row carries a colour/size (line 200 → api/products.ts:138). Each new variant is built with `stock: prev?.stock ?? 0` (line 252); `prev` is looked up by the generated variant id, which cannot exist yet, so every new variant starts at 0. The product's existing top-level `stock` (set by Inventory / CSV import) is neither carried over nor cleared — it is simply ignored from then on, because every reader keys off hasVariants: web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:210 (`stock = variant ? variant.stock : product.hasVariants ? 0 : product.stock`), admin totalStock (api/products.ts:29) and buildSkuRows (features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:197-212). The reverse direction (variants → none) IS guarded with an explicit toast at line 201-204; this direction has no guard and no warning.
failure_scenario: A published product has stock 50 and is selling. Admin edits it to add a Green/M variant with its own price and saves. Instantly the product list badge flips to "Out of stock", Inventory shows one SKU at 0, and the storefront shows "Currently out of stock" with Add-to-bag disabled — 50 units of real inventory become invisible until someone re-enters them in Inventory.
fix: When hasVariants goes false→true, seed the first variant's stock from the product's existing `stock` (and zero the top-level field), or block the save with the same style of explicit warning used for the variants→none direction.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, not refuted. In ProductFormPage.tsx onSave, adding any colour/size row to a previously simple product sets hasVariants=true (line 200 → api/products.ts:122,138). Each new variant is built with stock: prev?.stock ?? 0 (line 252), and prev is looked up by a freshly generated id against existingRef.current.variants, which is empty for a simple product — so prev is always undefined and stock is 0. saveProduct's update path (api/products.ts:194-206) never writes or migrates the top-level stock, so the product's real stock (e.g. 50 from CSV import at :314 or from adminAdjustStock's update.stock) is silently orphaned. I looked for a compensating handler and found none: functions/src has no products/{id} write trigger; adminAdjustStock (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:87-101) reads variant stock only when hasVariants && variants.length > 0 and never falls back to p.stock. Every reader keys off hasVariants and therefore reports 0: admin totalStock (products.ts:29) driving the "Out of stock" badge (:39), buildSkuRows (inventory/api/inventory.ts:200-212), web ProductDetail.tsx:110-111 ("Currently out of stock", Add-to-bag disabled at :295), ListingView.tsx:25, app product.dart:87, dashboard.ts:265. The reverse conversion IS explicitly guarded with a toast (ProductFormPage.tsx:201-204), which shows the direction is deliberately protected — this direction has no guard, no warning, and no carry-over. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Real, functional, and fixable (carry existing product.stock into the first variant, or block/warn like the reverse direction).

title: Product load has no error path — a failed read leaves the edit page on a spinner forever
detail: `getProduct(routeId!).then((p) => { ... setLoading(false); })` has no `.catch`. `setLoading(false)` only runs inside the fulfilled branch. If `getDoc` rejects — offline, an expired token, or a rules denial — the promise rejects unhandled (console-only) and `loading` stays true, so the component returns the spinner block at lines 279-285 permanently. This only bites when the products cache is empty (`seed` null at line 77-79), i.e. a hard refresh or a deep link to /products/{id}, which is exactly the flaky-network case.
failure_scenario: Admin pastes/bookmarks a product edit URL and loads it while the connection is dropping. The page shows a spinner and never resolves — no error message, no retry, no way back except the browser Back button; the console logs an unhandled rejection.
fix: Add `.catch((e) => { toast.error('Could not load this product.'); setLoading(false); })` (and ideally render an inline retry) to the getProduct call.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by direct inspection. ProductFormPage.tsx:107-136 calls getProduct(routeId!).then(...) with no .catch/.finally, and setLoading(false) occurs exactly once in the file (line 133) inside the fulfilled branch — nothing else can clear `loading`, so the spinner early-return at lines 279-285 becomes permanent on a rejected read. getProduct (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:79-82) is a bare `await getDoc` that does not swallow errors. There is no global safety net: no ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch/unhandledrejection handler anywhere in admin/src, and no persistent Firestore cache configured (no initializeFirestore/persistentLocalCache), so an offline getDoc rejects instead of falling back to disk. Reachability holds: /products/:id is a deep-linkable route (admin/src/app/router.tsx:66) and the seed cache is an in-memory Map (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts), so a hard refresh or pasted URL yields seed=null and loading=true. Not on the already-fixed list (that covers the auth listener, not this read) nor the known-intentional list. Two minor overstatements in the report that do not change the verdict: (a) a rules denial is not a realistic trigger since firestore.rules:50-51 allows product reads with App Check unenforced — the realistic trigger is network unavailability; (b) the admin shell/sidebar still renders, so navigation away is possible. The same missing-catch pattern also exists in CouponFormPage.tsx:87-90, corroborating it as an oversight. Fix is a straightforward .catch that toasts and clears loading (or a retry/error state).

title: Every product mutation control is shown to view-only sub-admins, and the rules cannot separate create from delete
detail: Nothing in features/products checks `modulePermissions` — grep for modulePermissions across admin/src hits only Sidebar.tsx:12 (which gates on `view` alone), QuickActions.tsx:42 and the sub-admin editor. So a sub-admin with products.view=true and create/edit/delete=false sees Import (line 160), + Add product (163), and the row menu's Edit/Duplicate/Archive/Delete (280-288). firebase/firestore.rules:52 gates the collection on `canWrite('products')` = `can(create) || can(edit) || can(delete)`, so every one of those writes is denied and the user only gets the generic catch-all toasts ("Could not delete X.", "Could not save the product.", ProductsListPage.tsx:122/133/143, ProductFormPage.tsx:273). Conversely, because canWrite collapses all three verbs (firestore.rules:31-33), a sub-admin granted only products.create can delete or archive any product — the server has no way to reject it.
failure_scenario: A catalogue-viewer sub-admin opens Products, hits Delete on a product, confirms, and gets "Could not delete Amber Oud." with no explanation (looks like a bug, not a permission). Meanwhile a data-entry sub-admin granted only 'create' opens the same menu and successfully deletes a live product plus all its Storage images.
fix: Gate the Import/Add/Edit/Duplicate/Archive/Delete controls on `modulePermissions.products.{create,edit,delete}`, surface permission-denied errors distinctly, and split the rules gate for /products/{id} into create/update/delete clauses instead of one canWrite().

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. (1) admin/src/features/products contains zero permission references (grep for usePermission/useAdminStore/authStore/admin?. across features/products, hooks, stores returns nothing), while QuickActions.tsx:42 shows the codebase's own correct pattern (gates on `create`) and Sidebar.tsx:12 gates only on `view` — so a products.view-only sub-admin legitimately reaches ProductsListPage and sees Import, + Add product, and the row menu's Edit/Duplicate/Archive/Delete, all unguarded. (2) firebase/firestore.rules has a single `match /products/{id} { allow write: if canWrite('products') }` with `canWrite(m) = can(m,'create') || can(m,'edit') || can(m,'delete')`, so those writes are denied for the viewer (surfacing only the generic catch-all toasts in ProductsListPage onDelete/onArchive/onDuplicate and ProductFormPage), and conversely a create-only sub-admin can update, archive, and delete any product. deleteProduct (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:44-50) also wipes products/{id} in Storage, and firebase/storage.rules:13 guards that with only isAdmin() — so the Storage-image half of the scenario holds too. Refutation attempts all failed: there is no server-side re-check (products are a direct-Firestore module; functions/src/catalog has no product save/delete callable, only inventory), no route-level module guard in admin/src/app/router.tsx, and the per-action permission model is real and enforced elsewhere (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts provisions modulePermissions; requireModule(req, module, action) is used with distinct 'create'/'edit'/'approve' verbs across orders, affiliate, notifications, customers, returns), so the granularity is a first-class product concept that the products module discards. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two imprecisions worth noting but which do not refute: the title says rules "cannot" separate the verbs — they can (split into allow create/update/delete), they simply don't; and the gap is systemic rather than products-specific, since canWrite is used identically for settings, content, categories, coupons, banners, flashSales, newArrivals, spinCampaigns and pincodes. That widens the fix rather than invalidating the finding.

title: Duplicate copies the source product's stock and reuses its Storage folder, so deleting the original breaks the copy's images
detail: `duplicateProduct` spreads the whole source doc (`...rest`, line 230) and only resets rating/soldCount/order/publish fields (lines 240-249). Two things ride along that should not: (a) `stock` and `variants[].stock` — the copy claims the original's physical inventory; (b) `images`, whose URLs point at `products/{sourceId}/gallery-*` in Storage (uploadProductImage, line 212). `deleteProduct` (line 44-50) deletes the doc and then calls `deleteStorageFolder('products/' + id)`, which recursively deletes every object under the ORIGINAL's prefix (lib/storage.ts:15-24) — including the objects the copy still references. The copy's `images[].url` then 404s on the list thumbnail, the edit form and the storefront gallery, and `variants[].sku` is duplicated too.
failure_scenario: Admin duplicates "Amber Oud" (stock 40, 3 photos), edits the copy and publishes it — the storefront now offers 40 units that do not exist and will oversell. Later the admin deletes the original; the copy's product page and every product card render broken/blank images with no way to recover them.
fix: In duplicateProduct, zero `stock` and each `variants[].stock`, and either re-upload the images under `products/{newId}/` or reference-count the folder before deleting it in deleteProduct.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Verified in /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:

1. Shared-Storage-folder bug is real and unmitigated. `uploadProductImage` (line 210-216) writes to `products/{productId}/gallery-...` and returns a `getDownloadURL` for that exact object. `duplicateProduct` (line 223-255) spreads `...rest` and never touches `images`, so the copy's `images[].url` point at objects under the SOURCE's prefix. `deleteProduct` (line 44-50) hard-deletes the doc and then calls `deleteStorageFolder('products/' + id)`, which (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/storage.ts:15-24) recursively `deleteObject`s every item under that prefix — including the ones the copy still references. Nothing re-uploads or rewrites the copy's URLs: ProductFormPage seeds `images` straight from the loaded doc (line 101/130) and `saveProduct` writes `values.images` verbatim (line 134), so opening/saving the copy does not migrate anything. No Cloud Function participates — grep of functions/src shows no product-write/delete trigger doing image copying, and no soft-delete path. The URLs simply 404 afterwards.

2. Stock ride-along is also real and reachable. `stock` and `variants[].stock` are copied. They are not fixable from the product form: `ProductFormValues` has no `stock` field, `saveProduct`'s `base` never writes top-level `stock`, and ProductFormPage deliberately preserves per-variant stock (`stock: prev?.stock ?? 0`, line 252, with the comment "per-variant stock/weight/visibility live in Inventory, not here"). Stock is authoritative at checkout — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:479/544/567 re-reads and decrements product/variant stock inside the txn — so a published copy really can sell inventory that does not exist. The only mitigation is that the copy is created as `status: 'draft'` and checkout rejects non-published products (checkout.ts:59), which merely delays the problem until the admin publishes the copy, exactly as the failure scenario states.

Both paths are reachable from the UI: ProductsListPage.tsx:129 (`deleteProduct`) and :139 (`duplicateProduct`). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. The duplicated `variants[].sku` is the weakest sub-point (SKU uniqueness isn't enforced anywhere I could find), but the images and stock issues stand on their own as functional, fixable defects.

title: Adjust stock can only be changed ±1 per click — there is no numeric entry, and it is the only way to set stock at all
detail: The Adjust column renders only two buttons calling `bump(r.key, r.stock, -1)` / `bump(..., +1)` (lines 149-157); the delta is a read-only <span> (line 152), not an input. There is no other path to set stock: the product form has no stock field, saveProduct writes `stock: 0` on create (products.ts:172) and never touches root stock on edit, and only the CSV importer can seed a non-zero stock (products.ts:314). So every unit of a newly created product must be clicked in one at a time, each click a separate setState + re-render of the whole (unpaginated) SKU table.
failure_scenario: Admin creates 'Kashmiri Saffron 5g' and receives 500 units. To record it they must click the + button 500 times on /inventory/adjust; there is no way to type 500, no way to type an absolute target count, and the click storm re-renders every SKU row each time.
fix: Replace the stepper span with a numeric input bound to the delta (accepting negatives), keeping the ± buttons as convenience, and optionally offer a 'set to' absolute mode that computes the delta client-side.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. AdjustStockPage.tsx:149-157 renders only two ±1 buttons; the delta is a read-only <span> (line 152) and `bump` (line 37) adds a hardcoded step of ±1 — there is no numeric or absolute-value entry anywhere on the page. I verified there is no alternative write path: saveProduct writes `stock: 0` on create (products.ts:174) and its edit branch never updates root `stock`; ProductFormPage explicitly preserves variant stock (`stock: prev?.stock ?? 0`, line 252) with a comment that stock 'lives in Inventory, not here'; InventoryListPage only reads stock and its row menu just links back to /inventory/adjust; ProductsListPage/FilterPage only filter on it. The CSV importer is not an escape hatch — importProducts always calls newProductId() and batch.set()s a new draft doc, so it can seed stock only for newly created products, never update an existing one. The backend is not the limit either: adminAdjustStock (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts) validates `delta: z.number().int()` and accepts any magnitude, so this is purely a UI gap and trivially fixable with a numeric input. Not on the already-fixed list (which covers adminAdjustStock's before/after return, a different issue) nor the known-intentional list. It is a usability/data-entry defect rather than data corruption, but since it is the only way to set stock for any product not created via CSV, recording a 500-unit intake genuinely requires 500 clicks.

title: StockHistoryModal turns any read failure into 'No stock changes recorded yet.'
detail: `getStockHistory(productId).then(...).catch(() => alive && setEntries([]))` — the catch collapses a permission-denied, offline or index error into the same empty array used for 'genuinely no history', and the modal then renders the definitive empty copy at line 54. There is no error branch and nothing is logged or toasted. `getStockHistory` (api/inventory.ts:168-173) is also an unbounded `getDocs` over stockAdjustments for the product with no limit, sorted client-side.
failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose custom claim has gone stale (or is simply offline for a moment) opens 'View stock history' on a product that has 40 recorded adjustments. The modal states 'No stock changes recorded yet.' The admin concludes the ledger never recorded their earlier corrections and re-applies them, double-counting stock.
fix: Track a third state (`error`) in the modal and render 'Couldn't load stock history — retry', and add a `limit(100)` with a 'load more' to getStockHistory.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. StockHistoryModal.tsx:25 catches every rejection from getStockHistory and sets entries to [], which line 53 renders as the definitive "No stock changes recorded yet." There is no error branch, no log and no toast, and nothing above it compensates: InventoryListPage.tsx:164-170 only mounts the modal, and admin/src has no ErrorBoundary, componentDidCatch or onunhandledrejection handler. The path is reachable — firestore.rules:230 gates stockAdjustments reads on isAdmin(), so a stale claim or a transient offline/unavailable getDocs rejection lands in the catch. This is also an outlier against the codebase's own convention: hooks/firestoreCache.ts threads FirestoreError through CollectionState (lines 21, 95, 117-118, 147-148) and features/reports/api/reports.ts:119 keeps cached data while surfacing the error; StockHistoryModal is the only place in admin/src that collapses a read failure into a success-shaped empty value. The secondary point also holds: getStockHistory (features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:168-172) is an unbounded getDocs with client-side sort and no limit. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and no other surface (web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared) reads or writes stockAdjustments in a way that mitigates it. Severity is lower than the reporter suggests — the inventory list shows current stock, so an admin would probably notice their earlier correction is already reflected before re-applying it — but the misleading definitive-empty-on-error state on an audit ledger is a real, cheaply fixable functional defect (add a distinct error state alongside null/rows).

title: A sub-admin without inventory.edit sees and can use the whole Adjust stock flow; the server's rejection message is thrown away
detail: There is no route- or control-level permission gate: router.tsx:71-72 mounts /inventory and /inventory/adjust behind RequireAuth only (RequireAuth.tsx checks `admin` truthiness, nothing else), and the 'Adjust stock' button (line 79) plus the row menu item (line 127) render for every admin. Only the Sidebar filters by `modulePermissions[item.module].view` (Sidebar.tsx:12). Server-side both adminAdjustStock (`requireModule(req,'inventory','edit')`, functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:26) and the stockAdjustments rule (`can('inventory','edit')`, firestore.rules:235) correctly deny — but AdjustStockPage's catch discards `e.message` and shows the generic 'Could not save adjustments.' (line 100). The same swallowing hides the CF's carefully written stale-SKU message ('N SKUs no longer exist … Nothing was adjusted — reload the page and try again.', inventory.ts:109-112).
failure_scenario: A catalogue sub-admin with inventory.view but not inventory.edit opens /inventory, clicks 'Adjust stock', spends five minutes setting deltas across 20 SKUs, hits Save and gets 'Could not save adjustments.' with no hint that it is a permissions problem — and their work is still on screen with no way to make it succeed. The same opaque toast appears when the real cause is a concurrently deleted variant.
fix: Gate the button/menu item on `admin.role === 'super_admin' || admin.modulePermissions?.inventory?.edit` (as QuickActions.tsx:42 already does for create), redirect /inventory/adjust for anyone lacking it, and surface `(e as FirebaseError).message` in the toast for 'permission-denied' and 'not-found' codes.

verdict.reason: Could not refute the core of it. Confirmed: router.tsx:71-72 mounts /inventory and /inventory/adjust behind RequireAuth only, and RequireAuth.tsx checks nothing but `ready`+`admin`; a grep of admin/src shows modulePermissions is consulted only in Sidebar.tsx:12 (.view) and QuickActions.tsx:42 (.create), so the 'Adjust stock' button (InventoryListPage.tsx:79) and row menu item (:127) do render for every admin. The decisive, non-refutable part is the error swallowing: the admin already has a shared helper /home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/cfError.ts that maps permission-denied to "You don't have permission to …" and passes through failed-precondition/invalid-argument messages, and it is used in ~15 other CF-calling screens (OrderDetailPage, ReturnsListPage, AffiliateListPage, CustomerProfilePage, SubAdminList/Form, AllocateAffiliatePage, ConfirmDialog). AdjustStockPage.tsx:100 ignores that convention and hard-codes 'Could not save adjustments.', discarding both the permission-denied code and the CF's deliberately worded not-found stale-SKU message (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:109-112). No interceptor rescues it: lib/firebase.ts is a plain getFunctions instance and adjustStock (features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:97) lets the callable rejection propagate untouched (only the ledger batch failure is wrapped as LedgerWriteError). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that entry covers adminAdjustStock returning before/after) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL. Caveat that lowers severity: the 'permission' framing overstates it — requireModule(req,'inventory','edit') and the firestore.rules stockAdjustments rule both deny correctly, so there is no privilege escalation, and no admin page anywhere gates edit-level controls, making the missing UI gate a codebase-wide pattern rather than an inventory-specific bug. The real, fixable defect is the swallowed message at AdjustStockPage.tsx:100 (should call cfError), with the missing disabled/hidden control as a secondary UX fix.

title: Stock is clamped to zero server-side but the ledger row still records the full delta, producing before + delta ≠ after
detail: adminAdjustStock computes `after = Math.max(0, before + delta)` for both the base stock (line 81) and each variant (line 92) and reports that clamped value back. The admin then writes the audit row with the ORIGINAL requested `delta` alongside the clamped before/after (api/inventory.ts:116-126, addLedger writes `before`, `delta`, `after` independently). The clamp is silent — no warning, no partial-application report — while the client's only guard is `if (current + next < 0) return d` against the possibly stale local stock (AdjustStockPage.tsx:41).
failure_scenario: A SKU shows 8 units in the admin's open tab; a customer buys 6 in the meantime. The admin records damage of −8. The transaction clamps 2 − 8 to 0 and the ledger stores before:2, delta:−8, after:0 — an audit row that doesn't add up, and 6 units of damage that were never actually deducted, with the admin told 'Stock adjusted for 1 SKU'.
fix: Either reject the adjustment when `before + delta < 0` (consistent with the batch-rejects-on-unresolved-SKU behaviour already implemented at line 108), or return an `appliedDelta` per SKU and have the client write that value into the ledger and warn the operator.

verdict.reason: Verified in code and could not refute it. functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:81 and :92 clamp with Math.max(0, before + delta) and return only {before, after} — there is no rejection, no applied-vs-requested signal. admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:116-126 then passes the server's r.before/r.after alongside the client's original a.delta into addLedger, which writes all three verbatim (lines 149-164), so a clamped adjustment stores before + delta != after. The clamp is reachable: the page's only guard (AdjustStockPage.tsx:41) fires at bump time against a live-updating r.stock and is never re-checked at save, while checkout.ts:570 / cancel.ts:126 move stock concurrently via FieldValue.increment. It is also user-visible, not dead data — StockHistoryModal.tsx:81-86 renders Change (delta) next to After (after), so a clamped row reads "-8 / After 0" implying a prior stock of 8 that never existed; and the toast at AdjustStockPage.tsx:91 reports payload.length (requested), so a partially applied batch still reads as full success. adminAdjustStock has only this one call path. Not on the already-fixed list (that item was about returning {before,after}, which is what introduced the mismatch) nor the intentional list. Confidence is medium rather than high only because actual stock remains correct — the impact is a false audit row plus silent partial application, not data corruption — but it is a real, one-line-fixable defect (delta should be r.after - r.before, ideally with a server-side clamp signal for the toast).
